root_cause.text: In the UFS core suspend path (`__ufshcd_wl_suspend()`), the `UFS_PM_LVL_0` case skipped flushing the asynchronous exception-event work (`hba->eeh_work`), allowing a race where pending exception handling accessed the host controller after suspend powered it down.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `ufshcd_disable_auto_bkops(hba);` and `flush_work(&hba->eeh_work);` specifically inside the branch where `req_dev_pwr_mode == UFS_ACTIVE_PWR_MODE && req_link_state == UIC_LINK_ACTIVE_STATE` before `goto vops_suspend`, and the CVE/commit message states that this configuration previously “bypassed flushing exception event handling jobs,” causing post-suspend host-controller access and crashes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable auto BKOPS and flush pending eeh_work before suspending in the active power/link state path to avoid suspend-time interference.
intent_record.what: In __ufshcd_wl_suspend(), two calls were added inside the branch where req_dev_pwr_mode is UFS_ACTIVE_PWR_MODE and req_link_state is UIC_LINK_ACTIVE_STATE: ufshcd_disable_auto_bkops(hba); and flush_work(&hba->eeh_work); before jumping to vops_suspend.
intent_record.how: When suspend is requested while the device power mode and link state remain active, the code now explicitly disables automatic background operations and waits for any pending eeh_work to finish before continuing the suspend path, reducing the chance of background activity or outstanding work interfering with suspend processing.

grouping_result.intent: Disable auto BKOPS and flush pending eeh_work before suspending in the active power/link state path to avoid suspend-time interference.

relevance_review.reason: The change explicitly flushes pending eeh_work in the active power/link suspend path, directly addressing the root cause race where exception-event work could run after the controller was powered down during UFS_PM_LVL_0 suspend.

candidates.rationale: This direct jump in the active power/link suspend case bypassed the newly added flush of pending eeh_work, enabling the race where asynchronous exception handling could run after suspend progressed.

vuln_statements.explanation: In the UFS_PM_LVL_0 suspend path, this jump transferred control directly to the vendor suspend handling and skipped the later-added flush of pending asynchronous exception-event work. That allowed hba->eeh_work to race with suspend and access the host controller after it was powered down.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the suspend-path control flow and the handling of the exception-event work. The root cause says the vulnerability existed when the `UFS_PM_LVL_0` case skipped flushing `hba->eeh_work`, allowing pending exception handling to race with suspend. In this snippet, the asynchronous exception work is explicitly flushed with `flush_work(&hba->eeh_work);` at line 8775 before the power-state transitions (`ufshcd_set_dev_pwr_mode()` at 8783 and `ufshcd_link_state_transition()` at 8794). Although the `UFS_PM_LVL_0` equivalent path (`req_dev_pwr_mode == UFS_ACTIVE_PWR_MODE && req_link_state == UIC_LINK_ACTIVE_STATE`) jumps directly to `vops_suspend` via `goto vops_suspend;` at lines 8733-8735, the vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the absence of the flush in the suspend path. In this function version, that flush is present in the normal suspend flow, indicating the code includes the intended handling for exception work rather than omitting it entirely. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present as an unflushed suspend path in the shown logic, and this version is best classified as already containing the fix.
